ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is an inscribed quadrilateral of the circle, with $AB$ as the diameter. It is given that $\overset{\frown}{DC} = \overset{\frown}{CB}$, and if $\angle DCB = 110^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle ABC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect AC, \\
$\because$ Quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in circle O, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$DAB + $\angle$DCB = 180$^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$DAB = 180$^\circ$ − 110$^\circ$ = 70$^\circ$, \\
$\because$ $ \overset{\frown}{DC} = \overset{\frown}{CB}$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$DAC = $\angle$CAB = $\frac{1}{2}$ $\angle$DAB = $\frac{1}{2}$ × 70$^\circ$ = 35$^\circ$; \\
$\because$ AB is the diameter, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ACB = 90$^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ABC = 90$^\circ$ − $\angle$CAB = 90$^\circ$ − 35$^\circ$ = \boxed{55^\circ}.

From the text, use ∠DCB = 110° and arc DC = arc CB. Since ABCD is cyclic, opposite angles are supplementary, so ∠DAB = 180° − 110° = 70°.
